newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - OCT 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - OCT 17.

text.p: CZECH REPUBLIC:

PRAVO - Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna now has 7,675,000 insurees, an increase of 888,000 clients according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus. The reason given for the increase was the recent decrease in the number of insurance agencies.

- The government approved a plan submitted by Minister of Trade and Industry, Vladimir Dlouhy, to financially restructure Aero Vodochody. A strategic partner for the aviation company should be selected by the end of this year.

- The government wants to help improve the situation with small domestic banks through a program which would purchase bad loans from these banks by the newly formed Czech Financial Institute according to Prime Minister, Vaclav Klaus. The condition would be beginning an individual stabilisation program.

- Pavel Tykac, the general manager of Motoinvest, a dominant shareholder in Agrobanka, stated that he saw indications that the Czech National Bank seems to have decided to decrease Agrobanka's basic capital, depreciating the shares of current shareholders and essentially nationalising the bank.
- Mortgage rates have increased substantially since this summer. The reason given for this is the Czech National Bank's July anti-inflationary measures concerning the entire banking sector.

- Neither Tatra Koprivnice nor Skoda Liaz will fulfill their ambitious plans to increase lorry production. Skoda Liaz decreased their planned output to 1352 lorries from the original 2200. Tatra decreased their estimates from 3000 to - The Radegast brewery, the second largest Czech brewery, has announced plans to increase capacity by 20 percent to 2,500,000 hectolitres from next March, when 12 new large-capacity tanks are to have been installed.
- The State Market Regulation Fund had purchased only 70 thousand tonnes of the planned 460 thousand tonnes of wheat.
- America's Gillette Company purchased 100 percent of Astra, the leading Czech producer of razor blades and shavers.

- The new passenger hall in Prague's Ruzyne airport, which will increase capacity to 4.8 million passengers a year, is expected to open to the public in June, 1997. HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The state may partially contribute to the easing of Tatra Koprivnice's debt of approximately four billion crowns.

- The government will likely decide on the privatisation process of Karlovarske Becherovka, the producer of Becherovka alcohol, by the end of the year. The for of the privatisation has been the center of debate for five years. The state owns 94 percent of the company.

- Centrotex a.s will become a significant shareholder in Jitex Pisek, the largest domestic knitwear firm with the purchase of a 30 percent block of shares from OB invest and approximately 10 percent from a public trade company.

- Germany's Landeskreditbank released an issue of Eurobonds in Czech crowns Tuesday. The issue, worth one billion crowns, has a fixed interest rate of 10.627 percent and matures on November 4, 1999. -- Prague Newsroom, +42-2-2423-0003
SLOVAKIA:

NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia said the reason for not paying its profit to the state budget in the first half of this year was its prorgamme of "monetary sterilisation". The NBS said it would fulfil its obligations to the budget in the second half of the year.

- The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, rejected fears that it would not be able to reimburse citizens for their privatisation bond in the planned year 2001 due to liquidity problems.
- The NPF said its share portfolio was now totalling some 90 billion crowns.
- Britain's Tesco Plc is to start complete reconstruction of the supermarket network in Slovakia bought this spring from the U.S. K-Mart.
- Singapore Airlines are to open their representative office in the Slovak capital Bratislava. The airlines, however, do not intend to inaugurate direct routes to and from Bratislava.

PRAVDA - Jan Gabriel, President of the largest Slovak bank VUB, said Slovak banks were undercapitalised and that the largest financial institutions, such as the VUB, would need at least to double their capital, for example through subordinated debts. Gabriel said VUB was negotiating unspecified offers from foreign banks, but that the bank would have to first stabilise the situation of its risky assets.
- Gabriel said Slovak banking sector was not threatened by a simmilar crisis development as in the Czech Republic.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Steel maker VSZ is attempting to aquire control over the investment fund Regionfond through its 20 percent stake in the largest insurer Slovenska Poistovna - holding 13 percent in the fund. Poistovna already initiated changes to the fund statutes and management, but the previous fund officials claimed the moves were illegal and took the case to court.
- According to the government plans Slovakia should have a balanced state budget in the year 2000.

- Export-import company Martimex, exporting about 20 percent of the Slovak engineering production, expects its turnover to total seven billion crowns this year. Martimex's main commercial partners are Germany, India, and the states of former Soviet Union, and the firm said it planned to expand its activities to China and U.S. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
POLAND
Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

Warsaw's heat and power generating plants want to invest in the mass media and leisure industries. Among other goals they are seeking shares in Nasza Telewizja (Our Television), a station which has won a licence for a trans-regional network.
Royal Dutch/Shell Group will formally open a liquid petroleum gas plant in the central city of Lodz. Shell Managing Director Steve Miller said Shell would invest $60 million in Poland next year.
The amended offer submitted by Polish-French consortium Hachette-Wydawcy Prasy for the Polish news-stand chain Ruch SA, is its final proposal, Gazeta Wyborcza learned unofficially.

The main failings of the 1997 budget draft are low spending on public safety, defence and the justice system as well as a growth of internal debt, says Adam Smith Centre analyst Krzysztof Dzierzawski.
Deutsche Bank Polska S.A. Chairman Georg Krapp said Warsaw has a good chance of becoming a major financial centre of Central Europe.
RZECZPOSP0LITA
Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz yesterday appointed a Civil Service Council to oversee administrative appointments. It has 24 members, politicians, officials and academics.
The European Union aims to devote 950,000 ECU for a STEP programme in Poland devoted to financing selected services for small and medium-sized companies.
The Progress National Investment Fund aims to prepare an issue prospectus.
NOWA EUROPA
A package of legislation for reform of the social security system will reach the lower house of parliament in March next year, Labour Minister Andrzej Baczkowski said.
PARKIET

According to unofficial information, clothes maker Zaklady Odziezowe Bytom, which has been offering investors 250,000 series B shares at 27 zlotys each since the beginning of October, will probably take advantage help from guarantees.
KPBP BICK plans to buy shares or stakes in other construction companies. It is especially interested in road builders.

Sobieslaw Zasada Ltd and Dailer-Benz InterServices Aktiengesellschaft opened a leasing firm, Mercedes Benz Leasing Polska with initial capital of 10 million zlotys. Sobieslaw Zasada has 25 percent of the shares, and the German firm holds the rest.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
